run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-16T16:18:39Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate warning for otel-demo/frontend-proxy reflects real 5xx responses returned by the frontend-proxy. Two distinct error populations were observed. (1) Before the checkout rollout, frontend-proxy had only sporadic 503 'UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' responses from the frontend upstream, at 9 log lines spread over 16:07:12-16:19:41, with ingress error spans of 1.1-4.4 per 5m; this is the most likely reason a threshold 'above 0' alert first fired at 16:18:39. (2) After 16:27:17, when the checkout Deployment rolled out a new ReplicaSet, frontend-proxy ingress error spans jumped to 34-169 per 5m between 16:29 and 16:39, and frontend-proxy access logs show concentrated 'POST /api/checkout HTTP/1.1' 500 via_upstream responses. The checkout cause is visible: the new Deployment sets KAFKA_ADDR=kafka:9999 while the kafka Service publishes only ports 9092 and 9093 (accounting uses kafka:9092); checkout logs show 'dial tcp 100.66.162.182:9999: i/o timeout' and 'kafka: client has run out of available brokers to talk to', the container exits with code 2 on PlaceOrder, the pod is not ready with a Back-off restarting failed container event, and the checkout Deployment reports Available=False (MinimumReplicasUnavailable). Kafka itself checked healthy (pod Ready with 0 restarts, Deployment available, Service endpoint present, normal KRaft log activity), so a broker fault is rejected.

claims.text: frontend-proxy ingress error spans (status_code STATUS_CODE_ERROR) were low but non-zero from the first sample: increase over 5m of 1.11 at 16:09, 1.25 at 16:11, 2.22 at 16:13, 4.44 at 16:15-16:17, 3.33 at 16:19, 4.57 at 16:21, 3.33 at 16:23; then 34.44 at 16:29, 115.56 at 16:31, 168.89 at 16:33, 152.22 at 16:35, 156.67 at 16:37, 103.81 at 16:39. These are span counts, not request counts.

In the 16:28-16:42 window the error spans concentrate on one call path: frontend-proxy 'ingress' (168.89 per 5m) and 'router frontend egress' (168.89), frontend 'POST' and 'POST /api/checkout' and 'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout' (170 each), frontend 'grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' (170) and frontend 'tcp.connect' (14.44); frontend 'GET', 'GET /api/cart', 'GET /api/data', cart, ad and payment operations returned 0 in the same query.

frontend-proxy access logs between 16:33:00 and 16:36:00 contain 109 lines matching a 5xx status; the newest 40 shown are all 'POST /api/checkout HTTP/1.1' 500 'via_upstream' responses proxied to the frontend upstream (100.96.4.193:8080), e.g. at 16:34:42.141, 16:34:47.045 and 16:35:43.745, so the proxy is returning 500 because the frontend answered 500.
The checkout Deployment container env sets KAFKA_ADDR=kafka:9999, while the accounting Deployment in the same namespace sets KAFKA_ADDR=kafka:9092.

The kafka Service (ClusterIP 100.66.162.182, type ClusterIP, created 2026-11-16T15:53:58Z) exposes only 'plaintext' port 9092 and 'controller' port 9093; it has no 9999 port. Its endpoints list one address, pod kafka-ff7884766-ntckh at 100.96.4.148, with ports 9092 and 9093.

checkout pod logs from 16:27:19 to 16:35:38 show repeated Kafka connect failures to that port: 'Failed to connect to broker kafka:9999: dial tcp 100.66.162.182:9999: i/o timeout', 'client/metadata no available broker to send metadata request to', 'kafka: client has run out of available brokers to talk to: dial tcp 100.66.162.182:9999: i/o timeout', followed by the config line 'kafkaBrokerSvcAddr:kafka:9999' and 'starting to listen on tcp: "[::]:8080"'. At 16:30:55 the log shows '[PlaceOrder]' and 'payment went through', then a new Kafka client init that times out again and closes the client.

The checkout container terminates with exit code 2 after those Kafka failures: pod checkout-849d65649b-qqtsz container 'checkout' lastState terminated reason 'Error' exitCode 2 finishedAt 2026-11-16T16:30:55Z, and at the later check the current state is terminated reason 'Error' exitCode 2 finishedAt 2026-11-16T16:34:22Z with restartCount 1 and ready=false; the pod Ready condition is False. An event 'Back-off restarting failed container checkout in pod checkout-849d65649b-qqtsz' is recorded at 16:34:23.

The checkout Deployment is at generation 2 with observedGeneration 2, replicas 1, updated 1, unavailable 1, readyReplicas null and condition Available=False with reason MinimumReplicasUnavailable; by contrast the kafka and frontend-proxy Deployments report available=1 and MinimumReplicasAvailable.

The failing pod belongs to a new ReplicaSet checkout-849d65649b created 2026-11-16T16:27:17Z whose pod template image is ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-checkout, the same tag used by the older ReplicaSet checkout-5dccddf8bb (created 15:53:59Z, now 0 replicas); events show the checkout Deployment 'Scaled up replica set checkout-849d65649b from 0 to 1' at 16:27:17 and 'Scaled down replica set checkout-5dccddf8bb from 1 to 0' with the old pod 'Killing'/'Stopping container checkout' at 16:27:20.

Before that rollout checkout was serving successfully: frontend-proxy access logs at 16:24:56.834 and 16:24:57.965 show 'POST /api/checkout HTTP/1.1' 200 'via_upstream' responses from the frontend upstream.

Before the checkout rollout, frontend-proxy's only errors were sporadic 503s with response flag 'UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' from the frontend upstream: 9 matching access-log lines between 16:07:12.890 and 16:19:41.802 on GET /api/products/* and /api/recommendations, each 503 with response body size 95.

Jaeger spans from 16:10:34 to 16:14:08 corroborate those 503s: 6 frontend-proxy 'ingress' spans are error=true with http.status_code=503 and otel.status_code=ERROR (durations 11.7ms to 564.3ms), each with a visible child 'router frontend egress' span carrying error="true" and http.status_code="0"; the matching load-generator GET spans record http.status_code=503.

Kafka shows no broker-side fault in the observed data: pod kafka-ff7884766-ntckh is Running and ready with 0 restarts, Deployment kafka is available=1, the kafka Service has a ready 9092/9093 endpoint, and its 80 newest log lines (16:34:31-16:35:37) show normal KRaft segment rolling, snapshot creation/deletion and retention activity without errors.

The frontend pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-n4sbv and the frontend-proxy pod frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-h7j7c are Running, Ready, ContainersReady with 0 restarts (containers running since 15:54:00 and 15:54:02), so neither proxy nor frontend pod is restarting while the 5xx responses are returned.

Across the sampled service set, error spans were non-zero only on the frontend/checkout path plus small flagd stream errors: ad 'flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream' 1.11, fraud-detection 'flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream' 1.11 (16:29), recommendation '/flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream' 2.05 (16:00-16:20), while cart, product-catalog, payment, shipping, email, currency and accounting operations returned 0 error spans in the queried windows.

The alert's initial firing at 16:18:39 was most likely driven by the sporadic frontend-proxy 503 UC (upstream reset before response started) errors on GET requests between 16:07 and 16:19, since that was the only error signal present before the checkout rollout; the underlying cause of those frontend connection resets is not established and the alert's exact expression could not be read.

The sustained high-volume part of the alert (error span increases of roughly 35 to 170 per 5m from 16:29-16:31 onward) is attributable to the checkout Deployment's post-16:27:17 setting KAFKA_ADDR=kafka:9999 pointing at a port the kafka Service does not publish: checkout cannot build its Kafka producer, the process exits with code 2 on PlaceOrder, frontend's grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder client span and POST /api/checkout spans error, and the frontend returns 500 on /api/checkout which frontend-proxy logs and counts as ingress errors.

A Kafka broker fault as root cause is rejected: the kafka pod is Ready with 0 restarts, the kafka Deployment is available, the Service has a ready 9092 endpoint, and the broker log sample shows normal KRaft log and snapshot activity; the checkout message is a dial timeout to port 9999, which the Service does not publish.

A frontend-proxy pod failure as the source of the 5xx is rejected: the frontend-proxy pod is Ready with 0 restarts, and its access logs record the 500s as 'via_upstream' responses received from frontend and the earlier 503s as 'UC upstream_reset_before_response_started', i.e. upstream behaviour reported by the proxy rather than a proxy crash.

The small flagd EventStream error counts on ad, fraud-detection and recommendation are not tied to this alert: they stayed at about 1-2 error spans per window and no frontend-proxy or checkout 5xx evidence references flagd.

Correct the checkout Deployment container env KAFKA_ADDR from kafka:9999 to kafka:9092 (matching the kafka Service's published plaintext port and the accounting Deployment's value), roll out, then confirm the checkout pod becomes Ready, PlaceOrder succeeds and frontend-proxy ingress errors return to the pre-16:27 baseline.

Review the checkout Deployment revision made at 16:27:17 (generation 2, same image tag 2.1.3-checkout) to confirm what introduced KAFKA_ADDR=kafka:9999, and reconsider the RequestErrorRate rule's 'above 0' threshold, since sporadic single 503s on frontend GETs already keep frontend-proxy's error rate non-zero.

gaps: The alerting rule definition could not be read: list_prometheus_rules returned no data for rule_name RequestErrorRate (view ca87cd9a-5251-40c2-91c0-3bd36e57c19c-t0:049a93f7-b94f-4485-8436-a6011c00fe02, status no_data) and for an unfiltered query (view d06bec46-3d1c-4beb-9fcd-932f67478d05-t0:fb773ce1-a4a4-4ab0-bb8f-03d095e1ecb0, status no_data), so the expression, lookback and threshold behind 'current: 1.7333333333333332' and the 16:18:39 firing time are unknown.

The cause of the sporadic frontend 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} responses between 16:07 and 16:19 is unknown: frontend container logs were not readable, returning no lines (views c2e0da53-6c73-4d25-9a12-4bd8896121ae-t1:767bda93-4b48-437f-8510-6521090de745, a0cfe95e-49d9-472e-be2a-c6a92002b4a7-t1:1a170b09-43d1-4213-be2a-ae334c5c11e2 and 67ba6c4c-77b6-465c-8127-a6f7c88869ba-t0:ea723602-52e7-49e5-9bc5-8087dc018b50, all status no_data), and the frontend pod shows 0 restarts.

No traces were retrieved for the 16:31-16:37 error burst and none for checkout at all: tagged searches for otel.status_code=ERROR returned no data (views 4e22450d-accf-4917-ab38-5be6f1f92a2b-t0:cdcf64fc-b2de-4b32-97a8-ac59a4970bd9, ca87cd9a-5251-40c2-91c0-3bd36e57c19c-t1:41269ec3-d1f1-4eb6-8c38-7d835cf8d36d, c2e0da53-6c73-4d25-9a12-4bd8896121ae-t0:a6c2f4e2-0a28-49e0-b819-f05701d2f7e0, 81277efd-b624-40fe-b5c0-3768e284564a-t0:764d773c-adeb-49b6-923b-494c569082b3, 5d795c55-e3e9-48b6-b1d0-32000fcc2cf2-t0:0218bf1a-beb6-42e5-9799-85e091fd52f4), so no span-level error message for the checkout PlaceOrder failures is available, and no checkout server spans can be cited.

A frontend-proxy trace search for 16:00-16:25 returned RESULT_TOO_LARGE (307 rows) and was not read (view ba7760f1-3bcb-48f1-9b61-bd11739c2408-t1:7fbf6b73-21d9-4773-945a-b4e32cdea092, status error), so that trace population is unexamined.

frontend-proxy access logs after about 16:35:44 could not be read (fetch for 16:36-16:42 returned 0 bytes), so the tail of the burst (16:36-16:40) is evidenced only by span metrics, and the fall back to 0 error spans in the final sample cannot be confirmed against logs.

kube-state-metrics series are absent from this Prometheus: the metric-name catalog returned 63 names with no kube_deployment_status_*, kube_pod_owner, kube_replicaset_owner or kube_pod_container_info, and a targeted query for http_*/kube_* names returned no data (view d06bec46-3d1c-4beb-9fcd-932f67478d05-t2:852f55a8-b271-4dd1-b2bd-5890fb5354d3), so container image digests and full label coverage could not be compared between the old and new checkout ReplicaSets.

The Kubernetes objects were read after the fact: the deleted checkout pod checkout-5dccddf8bb-9d9c8 and its env/logs cannot be read, so the pre-16:27 KAFKA_ADDR value is inferred from the successful 200 /api/checkout responses before the rollout, not directly observed.
The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so the author, mechanism and prior value of the checkout KAFKA_ADDR change (Deployment generation 2 at 16:27:17) could not be verified.

NetworkPolicy objects were queried and returned no data (view 6f687988-e4e6-46e8-a4e4-2329e1cd75bf-t0:7e99a884-e446-4877-bb9b-3defa47da432, status no_data), so the absence of a NetworkPolicy blocking checkout-to-kafka traffic is a gap rather than a checked fact.
next_steps: Change the checkout Deployment env KAFKA_ADDR to kafka:9092 and roll out, then confirm the pod becomes Ready, PlaceOrder returns success and frontend-proxy 5xx errors return to the pre-16:27 baseline.

Confirm through change history or CI why the checkout Deployment was revised at 16:27:17 with KAFKA_ADDR=kafka:9999, i.e. whether 9999 was intended and a Service port is missing, or whether the env value is wrong.

Capture frontend container stdout/stderr or enable file logging so the sporadic frontend connection resets (503 UC on GET) can be diagnosed, and consider raising the RequestErrorRate threshold above a single sporadic error or adding a sustained-error condition.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind.
